result: Reactome release 97, pathway and reaction summaries read through reactome.org/ContentService on 2026-10-21. Carnitine shuttle (R-HSA-200425): the malonyl-CoA-sensitive CPT1 of the mitochondrial outer membrane, the carnitine:acylcarnitine translocase SLC25A20 of the inner membrane and CPT2 on the matrix side of the inner membrane transport long-chain fatty acids into the matrix; CPT1A is most abundant in liver and CPT1B in muscle, and malonyl-CoA inhibits both; regulation at ACACA and ACACB minimises simultaneous mitochondrial catabolism and cytosolic biosynthesis of long-chain fatty acids. ACACB, on the outer mitochondrial membrane, regulates fatty acid oxidation through inhibition of CPT1 by its product malonyl-CoA, and phosphorylated AMPK inactivates ACACB in muscle cells (R-HSA-8876889, R-HSA-200423). Mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation (R-HSA-77289): repetitive removal of two-carbon units in four steps, oxidation, hydration, a second oxidation and thiolysis; each turn produces one NADH, one FADH2 and one acetyl-CoA. Beta-oxidation of saturated fatty acids (R-HSA-77286): the first pass for palmitoyl-CoA uses VLCAD (ACADVL) with FAD and the trifunctional protein with H2O, NAD+ and CoA, yielding myristoyl-CoA and acetyl-CoA; later passes use ACADL, ACADM, ACADS, ECHS1 and HADH; the seventh and final pass converts butanoyl-CoA to acetoacetyl-CoA, which yields 2 acetyl-CoA. ATP-citrate synthase (R-HSA-75848): fatty acid synthesis proceeds in the cytosol, while most acetyl-CoA is generated in mitochondria from pyruvate derived from glycolysis and reaches the cytosol as citrate, which ACLY cleaves; ACLY is highly expressed in lipogenic tissues such as liver and white adipose tissue and links carbohydrate metabolism to fatty acid production (R-HSA-9734540). ACACA, a biotin enzyme, is positively regulated by citrate (R-HSA-75851). Fatty acid synthase (R-HSA-75872): acetyl-CoA + 7 malonyl-CoA + 14 NADPH + 14 H+ = palmitate + 7 CO2 + 14 NADP+ + 8 CoA + 6 H2O. Synthesis of very long-chain fatty acyl-CoAs (R-HSA-75876): humans lack the desaturases to synthesise polyunsaturated fatty acids from stearate. SLC27A3 (R-HSA-8875077): members of the ACSVL subfamily were first thought to be fatty acid transport proteins (FATPs), but their transport function has never been proven, and their sequences carry two conserved acyl-CoA synthetase motifs.
